mainTopic: Whether a fetus can be made holy: why רבי יוחנן taught two rules, and רבי ירמיה's challenges to בר פדא's view, which רבי זירא defends using קדושת דמים and ולדי קדשים.
overview: The amud opens by finishing an explanation of why רבי יוחנן needed two rules. One rule is about making a pregnant animal holy, so the fetus becomes holy with its mother. The other is about making only the fetus holy. Each case has its own weak point, so each had to be taught. The גמרא then gives a second version (לישנא אחרינא). In that version, רבי יוחנן's point is that a fetus is not just part of its mother (עובר לאו ירך אמו), and again both rules turn out to be needed. Next, רבי ירמיה challenges רבי זירא with several sources that seem to show a fetus can be made holy, against בר פדא. רבי זירא answers that some of these sources mean קדושת דמים (holiness of value). He proves that this kind of holiness is still strong enough to cancel firstborn status and to forbid working the animal. He answers that the other sources mean ולדי קדשים, fetuses already holy through their mothers, which leads to a back-and-forth about תמורה, רבי יהודה, and limbs. The amud ends with רבי ירמיה asking why a משנה would say 'one makes holy' about offspring that are already holy, and the answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: Why the fetus case alone would not be enough
steps.stepSummary: If רבי יוחנן had taught only the case where someone made the fetus itself holy, we might think a fetus does not become holy when only its mother was made holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: [If he had taught only the first case, I would say it works there because he made] the fetus itself holy. But here, where he made its mother holy, the fetus would not become holy just by being part of its mother.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is in the middle of explaining why both of רבי יוחנן's rules are needed. This is the first half: why the fetus case by itself would not teach us the pregnant-animal case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the fetus case, the owner aimed his words straight at the fetus, so of course it becomes holy. In the pregnant-animal case, he only named the mother. Without a second rule, we might think the fetus is not included just because it is inside her.

keyTerms.meaning: A fetus, an unborn animal still inside its mother

phrases.english: the fetus itself.
phrases.notes: This ends a sentence from just before: in the first case, the owner made the fetus itself holy.

phrases.english: But here, where he consecrated its mother,
this one is not holy as part of its mother.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the צריכא answer that began before this section.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכא: each case has its own reason it might not work
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only a fetus named directly would become holy; one inside a mother that was made holy would not.
steps.terutzMaskana: So the pregnant-animal rule is needed to teach that the fetus is included.

steps.title: Why the pregnant-animal case alone would not be enough
steps.stepSummary: If רבי יוחנן had taught only the pregnant-animal case, we might think a fetus cannot be made holy by itself, since it has not been born yet.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he had taught us only the last case, I would say it works there because he made her holy along with everything inside her. But here, where he made only the fetus holy, it is not yet out in the world, so it would not become holy. That is why both rules are needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the other half of the צריכא. It shows why the pregnant-animal rule by itself would not teach us the fetus rule, and then concludes that both are needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Making the mother holy works on something already in the world, and the fetus comes along as part of 'everything in her.' Making only the fetus holy is harder, because the thing being made holy is still hidden inside. So the fetus rule adds something new: even an unborn fetus can be made holy by itself.

keyTerms.meaning: The last one, the second case
And everything that is in her
Outside (here, born and out in the world)
It is necessary: both statements are needed

steps.whatToRemember: First version of the צריכא: the pregnant-animal case teaches that the fetus is included with its mother. The fetus case teaches that an unborn fetus can be made holy by itself.

phrases.english: And if he had taught us only the last one,
I would say it is only there, since he consecrated her
and everything that is in her.
But here, where he consecrated it itself,
phrases.notes: "It" is the fetus, which he made holy without the mother.

phrases.english: since it is not outside, it is not holy.
Therefore both are necessary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the two-sided צריכא begun in step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכא: each case has its own reason it might not work
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A fetus that is not yet born cannot be made holy by itself.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both rules are needed. Each one teaches something the other does not.

steps.title: Second version: if a fetus is separate, why teach it twice?
steps.stepSummary: In a different version, רבי יוחנן's point is that a fetus can be left out of the הקדש because it is not just a body part of its mother. The גמרא asks why two rules are needed to teach that.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another version: What is רבי יוחנן teaching us? That if the owner left the fetus out, it is left out, because a fetus is not like its mother's thigh. If so, why do I need two rules?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a second version of the discussion. It explains what רבי יוחנן was teaching, and then challenges him: why say it twice?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here רבי יוחנן's lesson is that a fetus is its own separate thing, not a limb of its mother (עובר לאו ירך אמו). That is why the owner can exclude it. If that one idea is the whole lesson, it seems one rule would be enough.

keyTerms.meaning: If he left it out, it is left out
A fetus is not considered a limb ('thigh') of its mother; it is a separate thing

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two versions. Here the lesson is that a fetus is separate from its mother. In the first version, the point was whether the fetus becomes holy along with its mother.

phrases.english: Another version:
What is he teaching us?
That if he left it out, it is left out,
phrases.notes: "It" is the fetus. The owner said only the mother should be holy.

phrases.english: and a fetus is not the thigh of its mother.
So why do I need two?

steps.triggerLanguage: לִישָּׁנָא אַחֲרִינָא, מַאי קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a second version of the whole discussion.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's two rules: the pregnant animal and the fetus alone
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If both rules come from the one idea that a fetus is separate, one rule should be enough. Saying two looks like extra words.

steps.title: Both rules are needed: the mother gives the fetus a reason to be holy
steps.stepSummary: In the pregnant-animal case, the fetus might become holy only because its mother is fit to be holy. So we still need the rule that a fetus alone can be made holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both are needed. If it had been said only in this case, I would say the fetus becomes holy because its mother is fit to be holy herself, and since holiness comes onto her, it also comes onto the baby. But in the other case, with no mother being made holy, I would say no. So he teaches us this case too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 3 by showing that each rule teaches something new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a pregnant animal, the holiness 'comes down' on the mother, who is fit for it, and spreads to the fetus through her (מגו). When only the fetus is named, there is no mother to carry the holiness to it. So we need a separate rule to teach that a fetus alone can be made holy.

keyTerms.meaning: Fit in her own right, here meaning fit to be holy
Since, because (one thing happens, so the other happens along with it)

steps.whatToRemember: Second version: a fetus is not just part of its mother, so it can be left out. Still, both rules are needed. Holiness can spread to a fetus through its mother, but we also need to know that a fetus can be made holy all by itself.

phrases.english: Both are necessary, for if it had been stated only in this case,
phrases.notes: "This case" is the pregnant animal that was made holy.

phrases.english: I would say it is because its mother is fit in her own right,
and since holiness comes down onto her,
it also comes down onto the offspring.
But in the other case, no.
So he teaches us this one too.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'why two?' question from step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכא: the first case has a special reason (the mother) that the second case lacks
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A fetus becomes holy only through its mother, who is fit to be holy. A fetus on its own would not.
steps.terutzMaskana: The fetus rule is needed to teach that a fetus can be made holy even by itself.

steps.title: Why the fetus-only rule cannot replace the pregnant-animal rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא completes its answer. If רבי יוחנן had taught only the case where the fetus itself is named, we might think it is holy only because the person spelled out the offspring. So the pregnant-animal case is also needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if רבי יוחנן had said only this case (making the fetus holy), we might think it works because the person clearly put holiness on the offspring. But in that other case (making the mother holy), where he never mentioned the fetus, we might think the fetus is not holy. So both rules are needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes explaining why רבי יוחנן needed both rules. It shows that the fetus-only rule cannot teach us the pregnant-animal rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 showed that the pregnant-animal case cannot teach the fetus-only case. This step goes the other way: in the fetus-only case, the person named the fetus directly, so we cannot learn from it that the fetus becomes holy when nobody mentioned it. Since each case has its own weak point, both are needed.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed. This is the conclusion that both teachings are necessary.

steps.whatToRemember: Each of רבי יוחנן's two rules teaches something the other cannot. Making the mother holy also makes the fetus holy, even though nobody mentioned it. Making the fetus alone holy works too, even though it is not yet born.

phrases.english: And if it had been said only in this case (making the fetus holy),
we would say it works because he clearly placed
holiness on the offspring,
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets ("the mother") and some leave it out. Read it as "on the offspring."

phrases.english: but in that other case (the pregnant mother), it would not be holy. So both are needed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the two-way צריכותא begun in Step 4 by explaining the other side.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: each case teaches something the other cannot
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With only the fetus-only rule, we might think the fetus becomes holy only when it is named directly.
steps.terutzMaskana: The pregnant-animal rule is needed to teach that the fetus becomes holy even when it is not mentioned.

steps.title: A challenge from the משנה about cleverly avoiding the firstborn
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה challenges רבי זירא with a משנה. Someone can declare the fetus of a first-time mother an עולה before it is born, so it never becomes a בכור. That seems to prove a fetus can be made holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא sat and taught this teaching. רבי ירמיה challenged him: The משנה says, "How can a person cleverly get around the firstborn law? If an animal giving birth for the first time is pregnant, he says, 'What is inside this animal is an עולה.' If it gives birth to a male, it is an עולה." So we see that a fetus can become holy!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא is teaching the argument about making a fetus holy, and רבי ירמיה attacks the view that a fetus cannot become holy. He uses a משנה where a fetus is clearly made holy before birth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, a first-born male animal automatically becomes a בכור and goes to the כהן. The משנה says you can stop that by declaring the fetus an עולה while it is still inside the mother. This only works if holiness can take hold of a fetus, which seems to disprove בר פדא.

keyTerms.meaning: Using a clever legal trick to get around a rule
A first-born male animal, which is automatically holy and given to the כהן
An animal giving birth for the first time
A burnt offering, which is completely burned on the מזבח
So we see. It introduces a conclusion drawn from a source.

steps.confusionAlert: The "trick" is not cheating. The משנה permits it: the animal still goes to הקדש as an עולה instead of being a בכור.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira sat
and was saying this teaching,
Rabbi Yirmeya challenged Rabbi Zeira:
How can one cleverly get around the firstborn law?
An animal giving birth for the first time that was pregnant:
he says, "What is in this one's womb is a burnt offering."
If she gave birth to a male, it is a burnt offering.
So we see that a fetus can become holy!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new discussion: a challenge from a משנה against the view that a fetus cannot be made holy.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view of בר פדא that a fetus cannot be made holy
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה lets a fetus be declared an עולה before birth, so holiness must be able to take hold of a fetus.

steps.title: The משנה is talking about holiness of value
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא answers that the משנה means קדושת דמים, holiness that rests only on the animal's money value. So it does not prove that a fetus can receive full holiness.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said to him: When that משנה is taught, it means holiness of value (קדושת דמים).
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא defends the view that a fetus cannot be made holy. He says the משנה is talking about a weaker kind of holiness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two kinds of holiness. Full holiness of the body means the animal itself must be brought as a קרבן. קדושת דמים means only its money value belongs to הקדש, so it can be sold and the money used for an עולה. רבי זירא says the fetus in the משנה gets only קדושת דמים, which can apply to a fetus. That leaves room for the view that full holiness cannot.

keyTerms.meaning: Holiness of value: only the animal's money value is holy, not the animal itself as a קרבן

steps.confusionAlert: קדושת דמים is still a real kind of holiness. It is just weaker: the animal is not itself brought as the קרבן, but its value goes to הקדש.

phrases.english: He said to him:
When that משנה is taught,
it is talking about holiness of value.
phrases.notes: He means the fetus would be sold and the money used to buy an עולה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 6 by narrowing the משנה to a specific type of holiness.
steps.terutzResolutionType: אוקימתא: limits the source to a specific case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה proves a fetus can receive full holiness.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה only shows that קדושת דמים can apply to a fetus.

steps.title: Is holiness of value strong enough to cancel firstborn status?
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה pushes back. Can קדושת דמים, a weak holiness, really be strong enough to stop the animal from becoming a בכור?
steps.simpleTranslation: Is holiness of value really so strong that it takes away the animal's firstborn status?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה challenges רבי זירא's answer. He doubts that a weak holiness could block the automatic holiness of a בכור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the declaration stops the animal from becoming a בכור. רבי ירמיה argues that only a strong, full holiness could do that, not a mere holiness of value. If so, רבי זירא's answer does not fit the משנה.

phrases.english: Is holiness of value so strong
that it removes it from firstborn status?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in Step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי זירא's answer that the משנה refers to קדושת דמים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A weak holiness of value should not be able to cancel the automatic holiness of a בכור, so the משנה must mean full holiness.

steps.title: Yes: holiness of value does cancel firstborn status
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא says yes, and proves it from a משנה. Animals with a permanent blemish that were made holy get only קדושת דמים, yet they are exempt from בכורה until they are redeemed.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Yes. We learned in a משנה: All holy animals that had a permanent blemish before they were made holy, and were then redeemed, are subject to the firstborn law and to the gifts for the כהן. The reason they are subject is that they were already redeemed. But before they were redeemed, they are exempt. So we see that holiness of value is strong enough to remove firstborn status.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא answers רבי ירמיה's challenge. He brings a משנה showing that קדושת דמים really does remove the firstborn law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal that already had a permanent blemish when it was made holy cannot be a קרבן, so it only gets קדושת דמים. The משנה says such animals become subject to בכורה only after redemption. That means before redemption, their קדושת דמים alone was enough to exempt them. This supports רבי זירא's answer in Step 7.

keyTerms.meaning: A permanent blemish that makes an animal unfit to be a קרבן
They were redeemed: bought out of הקדש with money
The gifts given to a כהן from a slaughtered animal (the foreleg, jaw and maw)

steps.whatToRemember: קדושת דמים is strong enough to remove the firstborn law. So the משנה about declaring a fetus an עולה can be explained as קדושת דמים, and it does not prove that a fetus can receive full holiness.

phrases.english: He said to him: Yes,
and we learned in a משנה: All holy animals
in which a permanent blemish came before they were made holy
and they were redeemed
are subject to the firstborn law and to the gifts for the כהן.
The reason they are subject is that it is after they were redeemed,
but before they were redeemed, they are exempt.
So we see that holiness of value is strong enough
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is part of the corrected wording.

phrases.english: to remove an animal from firstborn status.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 8 and supports the answer in Step 7 with a proof from a משנה.
steps.raayaObject: That קדושת דמים is strong enough to cancel firstborn status
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about holy animals that had a permanent blemish before they were made holy: they are exempt from בכורה and the gifts until they are redeemed

steps.title: A pregnant animal may not be worked because of its holy fetus
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה brings a ברייתא. If someone makes the fetus an עולה, the mother may be shorn but may not be used for work, because work would weaken the fetus.
steps.simpleTranslation: He challenged him: If someone says, "What is inside this animal is an עולה," the mother may be shorn but may not be used for work, because the work would weaken the fetus inside her!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה brings a new challenge against רבי זירא. This ברייתא seems to treat the fetus as truly holy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא protects the fetus so carefully that it even forbids working the mother. That sounds like the fetus has real holiness, which goes against בר פדא's view, defended here by רבי זירא, that a fetus cannot get full holiness.

keyTerms.meaning: Using an animal for work, like plowing or carrying

phrases.english: He raised an objection to him: One who says
"What is in the womb of this one is a burnt offering"
the mother is permitted to be shorn
but is forbidden to be used for work,
because of the weakening of the fetus inside her!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge against the same position, after the first one was settled in steps 7-9.
steps.kashyaTarget: בר פדא's view, defended by רבי זירא, that a fetus cannot receive full holiness.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ban on working the mother to protect the fetus suggests the fetus is truly holy.

steps.title: This ברייתא is also talking about value-holiness
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא answers with the same answer as before. The ברייתא is about קדושת דמים, not full holiness.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: This too is talking about holiness of value.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא uses the same answer he gave in step 7. The fetus here has only money-value holiness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא agrees that a fetus can get קדושת דמים. So the ברייתא does not prove that a fetus can get full holiness, which is the only thing he denies.

keyTerms.meaning: Holiness that rests only on the animal's money value
This too, meaning the same answer applies here

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָא נָמֵי קְדוּשַּׁת דָּמִים.
phrases.english: He said to him: This too is sanctity of value.
phrases.notes: "Too" points back to step 7, where he gave the same answer.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָא נָמֵי קְדוּשַּׁת דָּמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: the ברייתא is about קדושת דמים.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ban on work shows the fetus has full holiness.
steps.terutzMaskana: The fetus has only קדושת דמים, which רבי זירא accepts.

steps.title: Can weak value-holiness forbid working the animal?
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה pushes back. Is קדושת דמים strong enough to forbid working the animal?
steps.simpleTranslation: But is holiness of value so strong that it forbids the animal from being used for work?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה questions רבי זירא's answer. He doubts that a weak kind of holiness could make work forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually only full holiness brings strict bans like no work. If קדושת דמים cannot do that, then the ברייתא must be talking about full holiness, and the challenge comes back.

phrases.english: But is sanctity of value so strong
that it forbids it for work?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 11, just like step 8 attacked step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי זירא's claim that the ברייתא is about קדושת דמים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: קדושת דמים seems too weak to forbid work, so the ברייתא must mean full holiness.

steps.title: Yes: value-holiness does forbid work
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא says yes. The משנה says blemished holy animals may be shorn and worked once they are redeemed. So before they are redeemed, work is forbidden, even though they have only קדושת דמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: Yes. We learned: they go out to regular status, to be shorn and worked. The reason is that they were redeemed. So before they were redeemed, they were forbidden for work. This shows that holiness of value forbids work.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא proves his point from the same משנה he used in step 9. He reads it carefully to find a hidden rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only permits work after redemption. That means work was forbidden before, while the animals had only קדושת דמים. So even weak holiness can forbid work, and the ברייתא in step 10 fits רבי זירא's view.

keyTerms.meaning: They were redeemed, bought out of their holiness

steps.whatToRemember: קדושת דמים is weaker than full holiness, but it still forbids working the animal until it is redeemed.

phrases.english: He said to him: Yes, and we learned in a משנה:
They go out to non-sacred status, to be shorn and to be worked.
phrases.notes: This is the משנה from step 9, about blemished animals that were made holy and then redeemed.

phrases.english: The reason is because they were redeemed,
so before they were redeemed, they are forbidden for work,

phrases.aramaic: אַלְמָא קְדוּשַּׁת דָּמִים אָסְורִין לֵיהּ בַּעֲבוֹדָה.
phrases.english: clearly, sanctity of value makes it forbidden for work.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the doubt of step 12 with a proof from a משנה.
steps.raayaObject: That קדושת דמים is strong enough to forbid work.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about blemished holy animals, which are allowed to be worked only after they are redeemed.

steps.title: The תמורה rule suggests a fetus can be made holy
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה brings a משנה: you cannot swap limbs for fetuses or fetuses for limbs. That implies only swapping fails, but making a fetus holy directly works.
steps.simpleTranslation: He challenged him: One cannot do תמורה with limbs for fetuses, or fetuses for limbs. It is only swapping that does not work. But making them holy directly does work!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה brings a third challenge, this time from the laws of תמורה. He reads the משנה carefully to find a hidden point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only rules out swapping with a fetus. That seems to imply that direct holiness on a fetus does take effect, which goes against רבי זירא.

keyTerms.meaning: Doing תמורה, trying to swap a regular animal onto a holy one

phrases.english: He raised an objection to him: One does not substitute
neither limbs for fetuses,
nor fetuses for limbs.
It is substituting that does not work,
but consecrating them, they become holy!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ: אֵין מְמִירִין לֹא אֵבָרִין בְּעוּבָּרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the ברייתא challenge is settled, a new challenge comes from a different source.
steps.kashyaTarget: בר פדא's view, defended by רבי זירא, that a fetus cannot be made holy directly.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה blocks only swapping with fetuses, which implies that direct holiness on a fetus works.

steps.title: The משנה is about babies of holy animals
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא answers that the משנה is about fetuses of animals that were already holy. Those fetuses are holy from their mothers, so this does not prove that a regular fetus can be made holy directly.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It is talking about the babies of holy animals, which are already standing in holiness.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא answers the תמורה challenge. He explains which fetuses the משנה means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The holy fetuses in the משנה got their holiness from their holy mothers, not from someone declaring them holy. So the משנה says nothing about making a regular fetus holy directly, and רבי זירא's view stands.
steps.whatToRemember: A fetus can be holy because its mother is holy, but this does not prove that a regular fetus can be made fully holy on its own.

phrases.english: He said to him: With offspring of sacrificial animals
it is that they are already standing holy.
phrases.notes: They became holy through their mothers, so nobody had to make the fetus holy on its own.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case: the משנה is about fetuses that are already holy through their mothers.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה implies that a regular fetus can be made holy directly.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about babies of holy animals, so it proves nothing about making a regular fetus holy.

steps.title: If the Fetuses Are Offspring of Holy Animals, Could They Make a Substitute Once Born?
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה challenges רבי זירא's answer. If the משנה is about ולד קדשים, it implies that once born they can make a תמורה, but a teaching says the offspring does not make a תמורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the משנה is about offspring of holy animals, then it only says you can't do substitution with them while they are in their mother's womb. That means once they are born, you can. But we learned that the offspring does not make a substitute!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה attacks the answer רבי זירא just gave in Step 15. He shows that it leads to a conclusion that goes against another teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says you can't swap with fetuses. If that is because they are fetuses, then after birth the swap should work. But a separate teaching says the offspring of a holy animal can never make a תמורה, born or not. So רבי זירא's reading seems to clash with that teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: The offspring of an animal that was already holy
Substitution: trying to swap a regular animal for a holy one, which makes the new animal holy too

phrases.english: If it is about the offspring of holy animals,
then it is only in their mother's womb that one cannot do substitution with them,
which means outside, one can do it,
phrases.notes: 'Outside' means after the baby animal is born.

phrases.english: But wasn't it taught:
The offspring does not make a substitute!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי וְלַד קָדָשִׁים, בִּמְעֵי אִמָּן הוּא דְּלָא עָבְדִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in Step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי זירא's claim that the משנה is about fetuses of holy animals
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה implies the swap fails only while the fetus is unborn, so after birth it would work. But a teaching says offspring never makes a תמורה.

steps.title: The משנה Follows רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא answers that the משנה follows רבי יהודה, who holds that the offspring does make a תמורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose opinion is this משנה? It is רבי יהודה, who said that the offspring does make a substitute.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא answers by saying the משנה follows a different תנא, רבי יהודה, who disagrees with the teaching that was quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The teaching that 'the offspring does not make a תמורה' is one opinion. רבי יהודה holds the opposite: a born offspring does make a תמורה. So the inference from the משנה fits רבי יהודה perfectly, and there is no contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: Makes a substitute (the swap takes effect)

phrases.english: Whose opinion is this?
It is Rabbi Yehuda,
who said: The offspring does make a substitute.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the משנה to a specific תנא (רבי יהודה)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's inference clashes with the teaching that offspring never makes a תמורה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה follows רבי יהודה, who holds that a born offspring does make a תמורה, so there is no clash.

steps.title: But רבי יהודה Says Limbs Cannot Be Made Holy
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה objects: the משנה implies that making limbs holy works, but רבי יהודה holds that limbs are not made holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the משנה is רבי יהודה, then it says only substitution doesn't work with limbs. That means if you make them holy directly, they become holy. But רבי יהודה said limbs do not become holy!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה pushes back on the new answer. Putting the משנה in רבי יהודה's mouth creates a fresh problem about limbs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only says you can't swap limbs. That suggests directly declaring a limb holy does work. But רבי יהודה is known to hold that declaring a limb holy does not work. So the משנה can't follow רבי יהודה after all.

keyTerms.meaning: Making something holy directly (declaring it holy)

phrases.english: If it is Rabbi Yehuda,
then it is only substitution that they cannot do,
which means if one makes them holy, they become holy,
but didn't Rabbi Yehuda say:
Limbs do not become holy!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, תְּמוּרָה הוּא דְּלָא עָבְדִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the משנה follows רבי יהודה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה implies that making limbs holy works, but רבי יהודה rules that limbs cannot be made holy.

steps.title: The משנה Means a Limb the Animal Cannot Live Without
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא answers that the משנה is talking about a vital limb, one the animal's life depends on.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: What case are we dealing with here? A limb that the animal's life depends on.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא answers by narrowing the case. The משנה is talking about a special kind of limb.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה's rule that limbs can't be made holy is about ordinary limbs. A limb the animal can't live without is different, and even רבי יהודה agrees that making it holy works. So the משנה can still follow רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? (a way of narrowing the case)
The animal's life depends on it

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is added by the corrected wording; some versions don't have it.

phrases.english: What case are we dealing with here?
With a limb that the animal's life depends on.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן — בְּאֵיבָר שֶׁהַנְּשָׁמָה תְּלוּיָה בּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 18.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seems to allow making any limb holy, against רבי יהודה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about a vital limb, which even רבי יהודה agrees can be made holy.

steps.title: A משנה Says You May Make Fetuses Holy
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה brings another משנה: one may make limbs and fetuses holy, but may not do substitution with them. This seems to show fetuses can be made holy directly.
steps.simpleTranslation: He objected to him: One may make limbs and fetuses holy, but one may not do substitution with them!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה brings a new source to challenge the view that a fetus can't be made holy directly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This משנה openly says 'one may make fetuses holy.' That seems to go straight against the position רבי זירא has been defending, that a regular fetus can't be made holy directly.

keyTerms.meaning: One does substitution (swaps for a holy animal)

phrases.english: He objected to him:
One may make limbs and fetuses holy,
but one may not do substitution with them!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ: מַקְדִּישִׁין אֵבָרִין וְעוּבָּרִין, אֲבָל לֹא מְמִירִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After Step 19's answer, רבי ירמיה opens a new challenge from a different משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The position that a regular fetus cannot be made holy directly
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה explicitly says fetuses may be made holy.

steps.title: This Too Is About Offspring of Holy Animals
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא answers as before: this משנה is also talking about fetuses of animals that were already holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, the משנה is talking about offspring of holy animals.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא answers with the same answer he gave in Step 15, and applies it to this new משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fetuses in this משנה already carry holiness from their holy mothers. So the משנה is not teaching that a regular fetus can be made holy directly. The position רבי זירא is defending stays standing.
steps.whatToRemember: Every time a source seems to say a fetus can be made holy, רבי זירא answers that it means the fetus of an animal that was already holy. That fetus is holy because of its mother, so it proves nothing about a regular fetus.

phrases.english: Here too,
it is talking about offspring of holy animals.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 20 using the answer from Step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (same answer as before)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seems to say any fetus can be made holy directly.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about fetuses of holy animals, which are holy from their mothers.

steps.title: Why say 'make holy' if the offspring are already holy?
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה challenges רבי זירא's answer. If the משנה is about ולדי קדשים, the word "מקדישין" makes no sense, because those offspring are already holy through their mothers.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the משנה is talking about the offspring of holy animals, what does it mean by "one makes holy"? They are already holy!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה attacks רבי זירא's answer from Step 21 by pointing to a word in the משנה that does not fit it. The word "מקדישין" ("one makes holy") doesn't work for offspring that are already holy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא said the משנה means the offspring of animals that are already holy. But the offspring of a holy animal becomes holy automatically, through its mother. So the משנה's language of actively making them holy has nothing to do, and that suggests the משנה really means a fetus made holy on its own.

keyTerms.meaning: The offspring of animals that are already holy (set aside as קרבנות)
"One makes holy": actively declaring something holy
"They are already holy and standing that way": holy already, with no new act needed
"If": opens a case so the גמרא can test it

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not whether ולדי קדשים are holy. Everyone agrees they are. The problem is only the word "מקדישין": you can't "make holy" something that already is.

phrases.english: If it is talking about the offspring of holy animals,
what does "one makes holy" mean?
They are already holy!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי זירא's answer in Step 21 by showing it does not fit the wording of the משנה brought in Step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי זירא's reading that the משנה about making fetuses holy means ולדי קדשים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: ולדי קדשים are holy automatically through their mothers. A משנה about them would not say "מקדישין" (one makes holy), since no act of making holy is needed. So the wording points to making a fetus holy directly.
